items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I left Earl and I went to New York to join Jimmy Lunceford... I got an opportunity to play a lot of solos. He had two good trombone players but they weren't really soloists... So, I got -- It was a good break for me going with him because I got most all of the solos to do.

ctx.x: long distance calls about your broadcasts, (Inaudible).

Yeah. That's right. I mentioned that. But one thing about Earl, he would let you grow in his band. He'd give you a chance to, you know, to develop. And this was hard to find in most bands because you had to have it when you got there. They didn't give you a chance to develop. And Earl gave all of us this opportunity. So, I think it was a stroke of good fortune for me going with Earl, and also the timing was good for me going with Jimmy Lunceford because as soon as I got in Lunceford's band, as I mentioned to you…
That wasn't your first recording with Lunceford though, (Inaudible) was it?
